chapter_text:
CHAPTER 13 — करुणापरा हि साधवः (KARUNAPARA HI SADHAVAH)

Introduction — करुणा किम्? परोपकारः किम्?

The very title of this lesson, "करुणापरा हि साधवः", means "the virtuous (साधवः) are indeed (हि) devoted to compassion (करुणापरा)". The word करुणा (karuna) means compassion — the tender feeling that arises in a good heart when it sees another being in pain, together with the wish to remove that pain. Its close companion is परोपकार (paropakara), formed from पर (para = other) + उपकार (upakara = help, kindness): doing good to others. A truly noble person (साधुः) is one whose heart naturally melts at another's suffering (करुणा) and who then acts to relieve it (परोपकार). In this lesson (NIOS Secondary Sanskrit, Course 209) we learn the meaning and value of करुणा and परोपकार, we read the classic public-domain tale of King शिबि (Shibi) who protected a frightened dove even at the cost of his own flesh, and we study famous Sanskrit verses that praise compassion and service. Along the way we build vocabulary (शब्दार्थ) and learn a little grammar (व्याकरणम्) — सन्धि, विभक्ति, शब्दरूप and धातुरूप.

Why compassion matters (करुणायाः महत्त्वम्)

Sanskrit literature repeatedly teaches that the highest mark of a great human being is not strength, wealth or cleverness, but a compassionate heart. The line "परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम्" ("helping others leads to merit; hurting others leads to sin") sums up the entire moral teaching of the eighteen Puranas in a single sentence. Compassion is called दया or करुणा; the person full of it is दयालुः or करुणापरः. Ancient teachers held that all beings — humans, animals, birds, even trees — deserve kindness, because the same life (प्राणः) flows in all. When we protect the weak, share with the needy and forgive the erring, we practise धर्म (righteousness) in its purest form. The good person lives not merely for himself but for others: just as trees give fruit, rivers give water and cows give milk for others, so a human body finds its true purpose in परोपकार. Compassion is therefore not weakness but the greatest strength — the strength to feel another's pain as one's own (आत्मवत् सर्वभूतेषु).

The story of King Shibi and the dove (शिबि-कपोत-कथा)

पुरा उशीनरदेशे शिबिः नाम राजा आसीत्। सः महान् दयालुः सत्यवादी धार्मिकश्च आसीत्। सर्वेषां प्राणिनां रक्षणे सः सदा तत्परः आसीत्। "शरणागतस्य रक्षणं राज्ञः परमः धर्मः" इति सः सर्वदा अमन्यत।

एकदा देवराजः इन्द्रः अग्निदेवश्च तस्य करुणां परीक्षितुम् ऐच्छताम्। अग्निः कपोतः (dove) अभवत्, इन्द्रः च श्येनः (hawk) अभवत्। श्येनेन भीतः कपोतः उड्डीय राज्ञः शिबेः अङ्के (in the lap) पतित्वा "हे राजन्, मां रक्ष, मां रक्ष" इति करुणस्वरेण अवदत्।

राजा तं कम्पमानं कपोतम् आश्वासयन् अवदत् — "मा भैषीः (do not fear), अहं त्वां रक्षिष्यामि। शरणागतं न त्यजामि।"

तदा श्येनः आगत्य अवदत् — "हे राजन्, अयं कपोतः मम आहारः। क्षुधार्तः अहम्। मम स्वाभाविकं भोजनं मा अपहर। परस्य आहारापहरणम् अपि अधर्मः एव। यदि त्वं मां क्षुधया मारयसि, तर्हि कः धर्मः?"

राजा चिन्तयित्वा अवदत् — "तव वचनं सत्यम्, परन्तु शरणागतस्य रक्षणम् अपि परमः धर्मः। अतः अहम् इमं कपोतं न त्यक्ष्यामि। तव क्षुधाशान्त्यै अहं कपोतस्य भारतुल्यं स्वशरीरस्य मांसं ददामि।"

श्येनः अवदत् — "यदि कपोतस्य तुल्यं (equal to the dove) स्वमांसं ददासि, तर्हि अहं सन्तुष्टः भवामि।" राजा तुलाम् (a balance) आनाययत्। एकस्मिन् पात्रे कपोतः स्थापितः, अपरस्मिन् पात्रे राजा स्वदेहात् मांसं छित्त्वा स्थापयति स्म। आश्चर्यम्! यावत् मांसं स्थापयति, तावत् कपोतः एव गुरुः (heavier) आसीत्। अन्ते राजा "सर्वं शरीरम् अर्पयामि" इति उक्त्वा स्वयम् तुलायाम् आरोहत्।

तत्क्षणम् एव देवौ स्वं दिव्यरूपं प्रकटयतः। "हे राजन्, तव करुणा अतुला, तव त्यागः अपूर्वः। शरणागतरक्षणे त्वं देहम् अपि न अगणयः। त्वं धन्यः, त्वं साधुश्रेष्ठः" इति उक्त्वा तौ राजानम् आशीर्वादैः अपूजयताम्। देवानां कृपया राज्ञः शरीरं पुनः पूर्णम् अरुजं (whole and unhurt) च अभवत्। शिबेः यशः त्रिषु लोकेषु अगायत।

शब्दार्थः (word meanings): पुरा = long ago; उशीनरदेशे = in the Ushinara country; दयालुः = compassionate; प्राणिनाम् = of living beings; रक्षणे = in protecting; शरणागतः = one who has come for refuge; कपोतः = dove; श्येनः = hawk; भीतः = frightened; अङ्के = in the lap; करुणस्वरेण = in a piteous voice; मा भैषीः = do not fear; आहारः = food; क्षुधार्तः = tormented by hunger; अपहर = take away (imperative); तुला = a balance/scale; तुल्यम् = equal to; मांसम् = flesh; छित्त्वा = having cut; गुरुः = heavy; आरोहत् = climbed up; अर्पयामि = I offer; प्रकटयतः = the two reveal; अतुला = incomparable; त्यागः = sacrifice; आशीर्वादैः = with blessings; अरुजम् = free of hurt; यशः = fame; लोकेषु = in the worlds.

English translation (सारांश-अनुवादः): Long ago, in the land of Ushinara, there was a king named Shibi, exceedingly compassionate, truthful and righteous, ever ready to protect all living beings; he always held that "protecting one who seeks refuge is the highest duty of a king." One day Indra, king of the gods, and Agni, the fire-god, wished to test his compassion: Agni became a dove and Indra a hawk. Chased by the hawk, the terrified dove flew down into King Shibi's lap and cried in a piteous voice, "O king, save me, save me!" Soothing the trembling dove, the king said, "Do not fear; I shall protect you; I never abandon one who seeks refuge." Then the hawk came and said, "O king, this dove is my food. I am tormented by hunger. Do not rob me of my natural food; taking away another's food is also unrighteousness. If you kill me by hunger, where is your dharma?" After reflecting, the king replied, "Your words are true, yet protecting a refugee is also the highest dharma; therefore I will not give up this dove. To satisfy your hunger I shall give flesh from my own body equal to the weight of the dove." The hawk agreed. A balance was brought; the dove was placed on one pan, and on the other the king kept placing flesh cut from his own body. But — a wonder! — however much flesh he placed, the dove was always heavier. At last the king said, "I offer my whole body," and climbed onto the balance himself. That very instant the two gods revealed their divine forms and said, "O king, your compassion is incomparable and your sacrifice unmatched; for the protection of a refugee you did not even count your own body. You are blessed, the best of the virtuous!" and they honoured him with blessings. By the gods' grace the king's body became whole and unhurt again, and Shibi's fame was sung in all the three worlds.

Moral (नीतिः): करुणा (compassion) and शरणागत-रक्षा (the protection of one who seeks refuge) are the very heart of धर्म. A great soul values another's life more than his own comfort — even more than his own body. This is why "करुणापरा हि साधवः" — the virtuous are always full of compassion.

Verses on compassion and service (करुणा-परोपकार-विषयक-सुभाषितानि)

1) परोपकाराय फलन्ति वृक्षाः परोपकाराय वहन्ति नद्यः ।
   परोपकाराय दुहन्ति गावः परोपकारार्थमिदं शरीरम् ॥
   शब्दार्थ: परोपकाराय = for the good of others; फलन्ति = bear fruit; वृक्षाः = trees; वहन्ति = flow; नद्यः = rivers; दुहन्ति = yield (milk); गावः = cows; परोपकारार्थम् = for the purpose of helping others; इदम् = this; शरीरम् = body.
   Translation: Trees bear fruit for others, rivers flow for others, cows give milk for others — this body too is meant for the service of others.
   Moral: All nature lives for the benefit of others; परोपकार is the true purpose of human life.

2) अष्टादशपुराणेषु व्यासस्य वचनद्वयम् ।
   परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम् ॥
   शब्दार्थ: अष्टादशपुराणेषु = in the eighteen Puranas; व्यासस्य = of (the sage) Vyasa; वचनद्वयम् = (there are but) two statements; पुण्याय = for merit; पापाय = for sin; परपीडनम् = the tormenting of others.
   Translation: In all the eighteen Puranas there are (essentially) two sayings of Vyasa: helping others leads to merit, hurting others leads to sin.
   Moral: The whole of scripture reduces to one rule — do good, do no harm.

3) श्रूयतां धर्मसर्वस्वं श्रुत्वा चैवावधार्यताम् ।
   आत्मनः प्रतिकूलानि परेषां न समाचरेत् ॥
   शब्दार्थ: श्रूयताम् = let it be heard; धर्मसर्वस्वम् = the essence of all dharma; अवधार्यताम् = let it be firmly grasped; आत्मनः प्रतिकूलानि = things unfavourable/disagreeable to oneself; परेषाम् = towards others; न समाचरेत् = one should not do.
   Translation: Hear the essence of all righteousness, and having heard it, hold it firm: do not do to others what is disagreeable to yourself.
   Moral: The "golden rule" — treat others as you would wish to be treated; this is the root of all compassion.

4) मातृवत् परदारेषु परद्रव्येषु लोष्टवत् ।
   आत्मवत् सर्वभूतेषु यः पश्यति स पण्डितः ॥
   शब्दार्थ: मातृवत् = like a mother; परदारेषु = towards others' wives; परद्रव्येषु = towards others' wealth; लोष्टवत् = like a clod of earth; आत्मवत् = like oneself; सर्वभूतेषु = in all beings; यः पश्यति = who sees; सः पण्डितः = he is (truly) wise.
   Translation: One who regards another's wife as his mother, another's wealth as a mere lump of clay, and all living beings as his own self — he alone is truly wise.
   Moral: True wisdom is compassion: seeing all beings as oneself (आत्मवत् सर्वभूतेषु).

व्याकरणम् — A little grammar (English explanation, Devanagari examples)

(A) सन्धि (Sandhi — joining of sounds). When two sounds meet they often merge or change. Examples from this lesson:
  • करुणा + परा → करुणापरा (आ + प; the words simply compound). Related दीर्घ-सन्धि: विद्या + अर्थी → विद्यार्थी (आ + अ = आ).
  • मा + अभैषीः → मा भैषीः (kept separate for sense) but न + अगणयः → नागणयः (अ + अ = आ) — "did not count".
  • परोपकारार्थम् = परोपकार + अर्थम् (आ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि). Split it back as परोपकार + अर्थम्.
  • श्रुत्वा + च + एव → श्रुत्वा चैव (च + एव → चैव, वृद्धि-सन्धि आ+ए=ऐ).
  Being able to SPLIT a joined form (सन्धि-विच्छेद) is a key reading skill, e.g. नागणयः = न + अगणयः.

(B) विभक्ति (Vibhakti — case endings). A noun changes its ending to show its role. Using the masculine a-stem model:
  • प्रथमा (nominative, subject): राजा/शिबिः "the king"; कपोतः "the dove", श्येनः "the hawk".
  • द्वितीया (accusative, object): कपोतम् "the dove (as object)", तुलाम् "the balance", मांसम् "flesh" — "gives FLESH".
  • तृतीया (instrumental, "by/with"): श्येनेन "by the hawk", करुणस्वरेण "in a piteous voice", आशीर्वादैः "with blessings" (plural).
  • चतुर्थी (dative, "for"): परोपकाराय "for the good of others", पुण्याय "for merit", पापाय "for sin".
  • षष्ठी (genitive, "of"): शरणागतस्य "of the refugee", कपोतस्य "of the dove", व्यासस्य "of Vyasa".
  • सप्तमी (locative, "in/at/on"): अङ्के "in the lap", उशीनरदेशे "in Ushinara", लोकेषु "in the worlds".
  Notice परोपकाराय, पुण्याय, पापाय are all चतुर्थी — the "for" case that expresses purpose.

(C) शब्दरूप (declension — worked example). The word कपोत (masculine, ending in अ, "dove") declines in प्रथमा as: एकवचन कपोतः (one dove), द्विवचन कपोतौ (two doves), बहुवचन कपोताः (many doves). Compare राम: रामः / रामौ / रामाः. The feminine word तुला ("balance") is प्रथमा एकवचन तुला; its द्वितीया is तुलाम् ("आनाययत् तुलाम्" — brought the balance).

(D) धातुरूप (verb conjugation — worked example). The root रक्ष् ("to protect", 1st gaṇa, parasmaipada) in the present tense (लट् लकार) goes: एकवचन रक्षति (he protects), द्विवचन रक्षतः (the two protect), बहुवचन रक्षन्ति (they protect). In the story the king says रक्षिष्यामि ("I shall protect", future/लृट्, उत्तमपुरुष एकवचन) and ददामि ("I give", from दा). The verb दा ("to give") in present is ददाति / दत्तः / ददति. Recognising पुरुष (person) and वचन (number) of a verb helps you find the doer.

SUMMARY (सारांश)

In this chapter you learned that करुणा (compassion) and परोपकार (service) are the highest marks of a साधु — indeed "करुणापरा हि साधवः". You read the public-domain tale of King शिबि of Ushinara, who protected a frightened dove (कपोत) from a hungry hawk (श्येन) — really Agni and Indra come to test him — and was ready to give his own flesh and whole body rather than abandon one who sought refuge (शरणागत-रक्षा). You studied the शब्दार्थ of the story and four verses on service and compassion, and drew grammar from the lesson — सन्धि and सन्धि-विच्छेद, the विभक्ति case endings (especially चतुर्थी "for"), a शब्दरूप model (कपोतः/कपोतौ/कपोताः) and a धातुरूप model (रक्षति/रक्षतः/रक्षन्ति). Let King Shibi remind you that the truest strength of a human being is a compassionate heart.

topics.name: करुणा एवं परोपकारः — Meaning of Compassion and Service
topics.description: What करुणा (compassion) and परोपकार (service to others) mean, how they are related, and why a compassionate heart is held to be the highest mark of a noble person (साधु) in Sanskrit tradition.

topics.name: शिबि-कपोत-कथा — The Story of King Shibi and the Dove
topics.description: The classic public-domain tale of King शिबि of Ushinara who protected a frightened dove from a hawk (Agni and Indra in disguise), offering his own flesh and body to uphold शरणागत-रक्षा (protection of a refugee).

topics.name: शब्दार्थ — Word Meanings and Vocabulary
topics.description: Building Sanskrit vocabulary through the word-by-word शब्दार्थ of the story and the verses: करुणा, दया, कपोतः, श्येनः, शरणागतः, तुला, परोपकार, परपीडनम् and their English meanings.

topics.name: करुणा-परोपकार सुभाषितानि — Verses on Compassion and Service
topics.description: Four authentic public-domain verses praising compassion and service — 'परोपकाराय फलन्ति वृक्षाः', 'परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम्', 'आत्मनः प्रतिकूलानि...' and 'आत्मवत् सर्वभूतेषु...' — with their meanings and morals.

topics.name: नैतिक मूल्यानि — Moral and Ethical Themes
topics.description: The moral and ethical themes of the lesson: compassion (करुणा), self-sacrifice (त्याग), protection of the weak and the refugee (शरणागत-रक्षा), the golden rule and seeing all beings as oneself.

topics.name: व्याकरणम् — Grammar (Sandhi, Vibhakti, Shabdarupa, Dhaturupa)
topics.description: Grammar drawn from the lesson: सन्धि with सन्धि-विच्छेद, the विभक्ति case endings (especially चतुर्थी 'for'), the शब्दरूप of an a-stem noun (कपोत) and the धातुरूप of a verb (रक्ष्, दा).

learning_outcomes.topic_name: करुणा एवं परोपकारः — Meaning of Compassion and Service
learning_outcomes.description: Explain the meaning of करुणा (compassion) and परोपकार (service to others) and describe why a compassionate heart is valued as the highest quality of a साधु.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: शिबि-कपोत-कथा — The Story of King Shibi and the Dove
learning_outcomes.description: Recall the events and characters of the शिबि-कपोत story — the dove, the hawk, Agni and Indra, the balance and the king's sacrifice — in correct sequence.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: शिबि-कपोत-कथा — The Story of King Shibi and the Dove
learning_outcomes.description: Explain the meaning of the King Shibi story and the idea of शरणागत-रक्षा (protecting one who seeks refuge) as the highest duty of a king.
Give the शब्दार्थ (English word meaning) of Sanskrit words drawn from the story and the verses and use the vocabulary correctly.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: नैतिक मूल्यानि — Moral and Ethical Themes
learning_outcomes.description: Analyse the moral or ethical theme of the lesson — compassion, self-sacrifice and protection of the weak — and apply its lesson to everyday situations.
Identify and perform simple सन्धि joins and splits (सन्धि-विच्छेद) using examples taken from the lesson.
Recognise the विभक्ति case endings and the शब्दरूप/धातुरूप patterns and state the case, number or person/role of a given word in the lesson.

learning_outcomes.topic_name: करुणा-परोपकार सुभाषितानि — Verses on Compassion and Service
learning_outcomes.description: Translate a given verse or sentence into simple English and answer comprehension questions about its words, grammar and moral.

chapter_summary.title: करुणापरा हि साधवः (Karunapara Hi Sadhavah) — Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This is the NIOS Secondary Sanskrit (209) summary for Chapter 13. It explains करुणा (compassion) and परोपकार (service), retells the public-domain tale of King शिबि who protected a dove even at the cost of his own flesh, presents four verses on compassion, and draws simple grammar — सन्धि, विभक्ति, शब्दरूप and धातुरूप — from the lesson.

sections.heading: Compassion and service — meaning
bullets: करुणा (compassion / दया) is the tender wish to remove another being's suffering; परोपकार (पर + उपकार) is acting to help others.
A साधु (good person) is defined by a compassionate heart — 'करुणापरा हि साधवः', the virtuous are always full of compassion.
Just as trees, rivers and cows live for others, the human body finds its true purpose in परोपकार and in seeing all beings as oneself (आत्मवत् सर्वभूतेषु).

sections.heading: The story of King Shibi and the dove
bullets: King शिबि of Ushinara was famous for compassion and for the vow that शरणागतस्य रक्षणम् (protecting a refugee) is a king's highest duty.
Agni became a कपोत (dove) and Indra a श्येन (hawk) to test him; the frightened dove flew into the king's lap for refuge.
To satisfy the hawk without abandoning the dove, the king offered flesh from his own body equal to the dove's weight — and finally offered his whole body.
The gods revealed themselves, praised his incomparable करुणा and त्याग, restored his body, and his fame spread through the three worlds.

sections.heading: Verses on compassion and service
bullets: परोपकाराय फलन्ति वृक्षाः...: all nature — trees, rivers, cows — lives for others; so should this body.
परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम्: the essence of the eighteen Puranas — helping others is merit, hurting others is sin.
आत्मनः प्रतिकूलानि परेषां न समाचरेत्: the golden rule — do not do to others what is disagreeable to yourself.
आत्मवत् सर्वभूतेषु यः पश्यति स पण्डितः: the truly wise see all beings as their own self.

sections.heading: Moral and ethical themes
bullets: करुणा (compassion) and शरणागत-रक्षा (protection of one who seeks refuge) are the very heart of धर्म.
त्याग (self-sacrifice) — a great soul values another's life above his own comfort and even his own body.
The golden rule and आत्मवत् सर्वभूतेषु teach us to feel another's pain as our own and to act kindly to all.

sections.heading: Grammar from the lesson
bullets: सन्धि / सन्धि-विच्छेद: नागणयः = न + अगणयः; परोपकारार्थम् = परोपकार + अर्थम् (आ+अ=आ); चैव = च + एव.
विभक्ति: प्रथमा कपोतः (subject), द्वितीया कपोतम् (object), तृतीया श्येनेन (by), चतुर्थी परोपकाराय (for), षष्ठी कपोतस्य (of), सप्तमी अङ्के (in).
शब्दरूप of a-stem कपोत: कपोतः / कपोतौ / कपोताः; धातुरूप of रक्ष् (present): रक्षति / रक्षतः / रक्षन्ति.

key_takeaways: करुणा (compassion) and परोपकार (service) are the highest marks of a साधु — 'करुणापरा हि साधवः'.
King शिबि protected a dove from a hawk even by giving his own flesh, teaching शरणागत-रक्षा — the protection of one who seeks refuge.
The hawk and dove were really Indra and Agni testing the king's compassion, and they blessed him and restored his body.
परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम् — helping others brings merit, hurting others brings sin.
The golden rule: आत्मनः प्रतिकूलानि परेषां न समाचरेत् — do not do to others what you dislike for yourself.
The truly wise see all beings as their own self — आत्मवत् सर्वभूतेषु यः पश्यति स पण्डितः.
चतुर्थी विभक्ति expresses purpose ('for'): परोपकाराय, पुण्याय, पापाय; सन्धि-विच्छेद splits a joined form (नागणयः = न + अगणयः).

glossary.definition: Compassion; the tender feeling that wishes to remove another being's suffering — the central value of this lesson.
Pity, mercy, kindness; a synonym of करुणा; a compassionate person is दयालुः.
Service to others (पर + उपकार); doing good to others, held to be the true purpose of human life.
A good, virtuous person; 'करुणापरा हि साधवः' — the साधु is always full of compassion.
The compassionate king of Ushinara who protected a dove by offering his own flesh; hero of this chapter's tale.
A dove; the frightened bird that sought refuge in King Shibi's lap (really Agni in disguise).
A hawk; the bird that demanded the dove as its food (really Indra testing the king).
One who has come for refuge/protection; protecting the शरणागत (शरणागत-रक्षा) is a king's highest duty.
Sacrifice, giving up; King Shibi's readiness to give his own body is supreme त्याग.
A balance or weighing scale; used to weigh the dove against the king's flesh.
The tormenting or harming of others; declared to be the cause of sin (पापाय परपीडनम्).
Merit, virtue earned by good deeds; परोपकार leads to पुण्य.
The joining/merging of sounds where two words meet; e.g. न + अगणयः = नागणयः (आ+अ=आ).
A noun's case ending showing its role; चतुर्थी (dative) means 'for', as in परोपकाराय (for others).
The conjugation of a verb root; e.g. रक्ष् (to protect): रक्षति / रक्षतः / रक्षन्ति in the present.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — करुणापरा हि साधवः (NIOS Sanskrit 209, Chapter 13)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give your explanations in English. Refer to the story and verses in the lesson where needed.

questions.question: Explain in two or three sentences what करुणा means and why 'करुणापरा हि साधवः' is a fitting title for this chapter.
questions.answer: करुणा means compassion — the tender feeling that wishes to remove another being's suffering. 'करुणापरा हि साधवः' means 'the virtuous (साधवः) are indeed full of compassion'. It is a fitting title because the whole lesson shows, through King Shibi, that a good person's defining quality is a compassionate heart that acts to protect and help others.
questions.explanation: Definition of करुणा plus the meaning of the title.

questions.question: Who were the दove (कपोत) and the hawk (श्येन) in the story of King Shibi, and why did they come to him?
questions.answer: The dove (कपोत) was really the fire-god Agni and the hawk (श्येन) was really Indra, king of the gods. They took these forms to test King Shibi's compassion (करुणा) and his vow to protect anyone who sought his refuge.
questions.explanation: Agni = dove, Indra = hawk; they came to test the king's compassion.

questions.question: What is शरणागत-रक्षा, and how did King Shibi uphold it?
questions.answer: शरणागत-रक्षा means the protection of one who has come seeking refuge. King Shibi upheld it by refusing to hand over the frightened dove to the hawk, even when it meant cutting flesh from his own body — and finally offering his whole body — rather than abandon a creature that had sought his protection.
questions.explanation: Definition plus the king's action of self-sacrifice.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English word meaning) of each: कपोतः, श्येनः, तुला, मांसम्, दयालुः.
questions.answer: कपोतः = dove; श्येनः = hawk; तुला = balance/scale; मांसम् = flesh; दयालुः = compassionate/kind.

questions.question: Translate into simple English and state the moral: 'परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम्'.
questions.answer: Translation: Helping others (परोपकार) leads to merit (पुण्य); tormenting others (परपीडन) leads to sin (पाप). Moral: the essence of all scripture is simply to do good to others and to harm no one.
questions.explanation: Vyasa's two-line summary of the eighteen Puranas.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद (split) of: (a) नागणयः (b) परोपकारार्थम्.
questions.answer: (a) नागणयः = न + अगणयः (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि). (b) परोपकारार्थम् = परोपकार + अर्थम् (आ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि).
questions.explanation: Splitting a joined form back into its words is सन्धि-विच्छेद.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति (case) and its meaning-role for each: परोपकाराय, श्येनेन, कपोतस्य.
questions.answer: परोपकाराय = चतुर्थी (dative) → 'for the good of others'. श्येनेन = तृतीया (instrumental) → 'by the hawk'. कपोतस्य = षष्ठी (genitive) → 'of the dove'.
questions.explanation: चतुर्थी shows purpose/for, तृतीया shows means/by, षष्ठी shows possession/of.

questions.question: Retell the story of King Shibi and the dove in your own words (5-6 sentences) and explain the value it teaches.
questions.answer: Long ago King Shibi of Ushinara was famous for compassion and held that protecting a refugee is a king's highest duty. To test him, Agni became a dove and Indra a hawk. Chased by the hawk, the terrified dove flew into the king's lap and begged for protection, and the king promised to save it. The hawk protested that the dove was its lawful food and that starving it would also be unrighteous. To satisfy the hawk without abandoning the dove, the king offered flesh from his own body equal to the dove's weight, but the dove always weighed more, so at last he offered his whole body. The gods then revealed themselves, praised his incomparable compassion and sacrifice, and restored his body. The story teaches करुणा (compassion), शरणागत-रक्षा (protecting one who seeks refuge) and त्याग (self-sacrifice) as the heart of dharma.
questions.explanation: Full narrative plus the values of compassion, refuge-protection and sacrifice.

questions.question: The verse says 'आत्मनः प्रतिकूलानि परेषां न समाचरेत्'. Explain this 'golden rule' and give three ways a student can practise it today.
questions.answer: The verse means: do not do to others what is disagreeable to yourself. This is called the essence of all dharma (धर्मसर्वस्व) — since I dislike being hurt, cheated or insulted, I should not hurt, cheat or insult others. A student can practise it by: (1) speaking to classmates and juniors the way he would like to be spoken to, not mocking or bullying; (2) not taking or damaging others' belongings, because he would not want his own taken; (3) helping a friend in difficulty, since he too would want help when in trouble. Practising this rule turns knowledge into real compassion (करुणा).
questions.explanation: Explanation of the golden rule plus three practical applications.

questions.question: Give the धातुरूप (present tense, three numbers) of the root रक्ष् ('to protect') and say what पुरुष/वचन 'रक्षिष्यामि' is.
questions.answer: रक्ष् (present/लट्, parasmaipada, प्रथमपुरुष): एकवचन रक्षति, द्विवचन रक्षतः, बहुवचन रक्षन्ति. 'रक्षिष्यामि' ('I shall protect') is उत्तमपुरुष एकवचन in the future (लृट्) tense.
questions.explanation: Basic धातुरूप of रक्ष् and person/number of रक्षिष्यामि.

questions.answer: परोपकार (पर + उपकार) means doing good to others, service to others. Example from the verse: trees (वृक्षाः) bear fruit for the good of others (परोपकाराय), not for themselves.

questions.question: How are करुणा and परोपकार related?
questions.answer: करुणा (compassion) is the tender feeling in the heart that wishes to remove another's suffering; परोपकार is the action of actually helping others. Compassion is the feeling and service is its action — करुणा leads naturally to परोपकार.
questions.explanation: करुणा = feeling; परोपकार = the resulting action.

questions.question: Name the four divine/animal characters in the Shibi story and what each really was.
questions.answer: The dove (कपोत) was really the fire-god Agni; the hawk (श्येन) was really Indra, king of the gods. They came in these forms to test King Shibi's compassion.
questions.explanation: Dove=Agni, Hawk=Indra; they test the king.

questions.question: Describe in two or three sentences what happened at the balance (तुला).
questions.answer: The dove was placed on one pan of the balance and the king cut flesh from his own body to place on the other pan. However much flesh he placed, the dove always weighed more, so at last the king climbed onto the balance to offer his whole body.
questions.explanation: The dove always outweighed the flesh, so the king offered himself.

questions.question: Why did the king refuse to give the dove to the hawk even though he pitied the hungry hawk?
questions.answer: Because protecting one who has come for refuge (शरणागत-रक्षा) is a king's highest duty, and the dove had sought his protection. Instead of abandoning the refugee, the king chose to satisfy the hawk's hunger with flesh from his own body.
questions.explanation: Refuge-protection is supreme; he fed the hawk from his own body.

questions.question: The hawk said starving it would also be adharma. How did the king honour both duties?
questions.answer: The king accepted that letting the hawk starve would be wrong, but he would not abandon the dove either. He honoured both duties by giving flesh from his own body equal to the dove's weight — protecting the refugee while still feeding the hungry hawk.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: शरणागतः, आहारः, यशः, त्यागः.
questions.answer: शरणागतः = one who has come for refuge; आहारः = food; यशः = fame/glory; त्यागः = sacrifice/renunciation.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: परपीडनम्, पुण्यम्, वचनद्वयम्, अष्टादशपुराणेषु.
questions.answer: परपीडनम् = harming/tormenting others; पुण्यम् = merit; वचनद्वयम् = two statements/a pair of sayings; अष्टादशपुराणेषु = in the eighteen Puranas.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: दयालुः, क्षुधार्तः, गुरुः, तुला.
questions.answer: दयालुः = compassionate; क्षुधार्तः = tormented by hunger; गुरुः = heavy; तुला = balance/scale.

questions.question: Translate into English: 'परोपकाराय फलन्ति वृक्षाः परोपकाराय वहन्ति नद्यः'.
questions.answer: Trees (वृक्षाः) bear fruit for the good of others (परोपकाराय); rivers (नद्यः) flow for the good of others.

questions.question: Translate into English: 'आत्मवत् सर्वभूतेषु यः पश्यति स पण्डितः'.
questions.answer: He who sees all living beings (सर्वभूतेषु) as his own self (आत्मवत्) — he is (truly) wise (पण्डितः).
questions.explanation: True wisdom is seeing all as oneself.

questions.question: Translate into English: 'शरणागतस्य रक्षणं राज्ञः परमः धर्मः'.
questions.answer: The protection (रक्षणम्) of one who has come for refuge (शरणागतस्य) is the highest duty (परमः धर्मः) of a king (राज्ञः).
questions.explanation: Refuge-protection is the king's highest dharma.

questions.question: Write two simple Sanskrit sentences (in Devanagari) about compassion, with English meanings.
questions.answer: 1. साधुः सर्वेषु प्राणिषु दयां करोति। (The good person shows compassion to all living beings.) 2. वयं परोपकारं कुर्मः। (We do service to others.)

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of: (a) करुणापरा (b) चैव.
questions.answer: (a) करुणापरा = करुणा + परा. (b) चैव = च + एव (अ + ए = ऐ, वृद्धि-सन्धि).

questions.question: What is सन्धि? What is सन्धि-विच्छेद? Give one example.
questions.answer: सन्धि is the joining/merging of sounds where two words meet (e.g. न + अगणयः = नागणयः). सन्धि-विच्छेद is the reverse — splitting a joined form back into its separate words (नागणयः = न + अगणयः).
questions.explanation: Definition of सन्धि and its splitting.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति and role of: परोपकाराय, अङ्के, मांसम्.
questions.answer: परोपकाराय = चतुर्थी (dative) → 'for the good of others'. अङ्के = सप्तमी (locative) → 'in the lap'. मांसम् = द्वितीया (accusative) → 'flesh' (as object).
questions.explanation: Dative for purpose, locative for place, accusative for object.

questions.question: Give the प्रथमा (एक/द्वि/बहु) forms of कपोत and the present-tense forms of रक्ष्.
questions.answer: कपोत (प्रथमा): कपोतः / कपोतौ / कपोताः. रक्ष् (present, प्रथमपुरुष): रक्षति / रक्षतः / रक्षन्ति.

questions.question: What moral does the verse 'परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम्' teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that the whole of scripture reduces to two things: doing good to others (परोपकार) earns merit (पुण्य), and harming others (परपीडन) causes sin (पाप). So we should always help and never harm.

questions.question: How can the value of King Shibi's compassion be applied in modern life?
questions.answer: By protecting and helping those who are weak or in trouble — standing up for someone being bullied, sheltering or feeding the needy, being kind to animals, and putting others' genuine needs before one's own comfort. Like Shibi, we should not abandon anyone who comes to us for help.
questions.explanation: Protect the weak; help those who seek our aid.

questions.question: Why does the lesson say a compassionate heart is the greatest strength, not weakness?
questions.answer: Because it takes real inner strength to feel another's pain as one's own and to sacrifice one's own comfort — even one's body, as Shibi did — for another's sake. Cruelty is easy; compassion that acts and sacrifices requires courage and greatness of soul.
questions.explanation: Compassion that acts and sacrifices is true strength.

questions.question: What did the gods do at the end of the story, and what does it show?
questions.answer: The gods revealed their true forms, praised King Shibi's incomparable compassion and sacrifice, blessed him and restored his body to full health. It shows that selfless compassion is honoured even by the gods and never goes unrewarded.
questions.explanation: The gods bless and restore the king.

questions.question: In which country did King Shibi rule, and for what quality was he famous?
questions.answer: King Shibi ruled the country of Ushinara (उशीनर). He was famous for his compassion (करुणा/दया), truthfulness and his vow to protect anyone who sought his refuge.
questions.explanation: Ushinara; famous for compassion and refuge-protection.

questions.question: Narrate the full story of King Shibi and the dove in your own words and state the values it teaches.
questions.answer: Long ago King Shibi of Ushinara was renowned for compassion, truth and righteousness, and he firmly believed that protecting one who seeks refuge is a king's highest duty. To test him, Agni took the form of a dove and Indra the form of a hawk. Chased by the hawk, the frightened dove flew into the king's lap and begged, 'Save me!' The king comforted it and promised protection. The hawk then arrived and argued that the dove was its natural food and that to starve it would also be unrighteous. Caught between two duties, the king refused to give up the refugee dove but offered instead flesh from his own body equal to the dove's weight. When the dove kept outweighing the flesh, the king finally offered his whole body upon the balance. At once the gods revealed themselves, praised his incomparable compassion and sacrifice, restored his body, and his fame spread through the three worlds. The story teaches करुणा (compassion), शरणागत-रक्षा (protection of one who seeks refuge) and त्याग (selfless sacrifice).
questions.explanation: Complete narration with the three core values.

questions.question: 'करुणापरा हि साधवः.' Discuss, using the story and the verses, why compassion is regarded as the highest virtue.
questions.answer: The phrase 'करुणापरा हि साधवः' means the virtuous are always full of compassion, and the whole lesson shows why compassion (करुणा) is prized above all. King Shibi's story proves that true greatness is measured not by power or wealth but by how far one will go to relieve another's suffering — he was ready to give his own flesh and body for a small dove. The verse 'परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम्' declares that the essence of all scripture is to help others and harm none, so compassion is the root of all merit. 'आत्मनः प्रतिकूलानि परेषां न समाचरेत्' (the golden rule) and 'आत्मवत् सर्वभूतेषु यः पश्यति स पण्डितः' add that real wisdom is to feel others' pain as one's own. Because compassion protects the weak, binds society in kindness and turns knowledge into good action, it is regarded as the highest virtue of a साधु.
questions.explanation: Uses story + verses to justify compassion as supreme virtue.

questions.question: Translate the verse 'श्रूयतां धर्मसर्वस्वं श्रुत्वा चैवावधार्यताम्, आत्मनः प्रतिकूलानि परेषां न समाचरेत्' and explain its meaning with an example.
questions.answer: Translation: 'Hear the essence of all dharma (धर्मसर्वस्वम्), and having heard it, hold it firm: do not do to others (परेषाम्) what is disagreeable (प्रतिकूलानि) to yourself (आत्मनः).' Meaning: this is the famous golden rule — since I do not like to be hurt, cheated or spoken to rudely, I must not treat others in those ways. Example: if I would feel bad when someone laughs at my mistake, then I should not laugh at a classmate's mistake; instead I should help him. The verse compresses all of dharma into this single principle of compassion.
questions.explanation: Translation plus the golden rule with an example.

questions.question: List and give the शब्दार्थ of at least eight important words from this lesson.
questions.answer: 1. करुणा = compassion. 2. दया = mercy/pity. 3. परोपकार = service to others. 4. कपोतः = dove. 5. श्येनः = hawk. 6. शरणागतः = one who seeks refuge. 7. तुला = balance/scale. 8. मांसम् = flesh. 9. त्यागः = sacrifice. 10. परपीडनम् = harming others. 11. पुण्यम् = merit. 12. यशः = fame.

questions.question: Explain, with the verse 'परोपकाराय फलन्ति वृक्षाः...', how nature teaches the lesson of service.
questions.answer: The verse says trees (वृक्षाः) bear fruit for others, rivers (नद्यः) flow for others, and cows (गावः) give milk for others (परोपकाराय) — and concludes that this human body too is meant for the service of others (परोपकारार्थमिदं शरीरम्). Nature is the great teacher of परोपकार: a tree does not eat its own fruit, a river does not drink its own water, a cow does not keep its own milk; each exists to nourish others. The verse urges human beings to follow nature's example and to live not selfishly but for the good of all. Thus even the body, our most personal possession, finds its true purpose in compassion and service.
questions.explanation: Uses the nature imagery to explain परोपकार.

questions.question: Describe the character of King Shibi as shown in this lesson.
questions.answer: King Shibi of Ushinara is shown as an ideal king: he is दयालु (compassionate), सत्यवादी (truthful) and धार्मिक (righteous). He is ever ready to protect all living beings and firmly holds that protecting one who seeks refuge is his highest duty. He is calm and thoughtful — he listens even to the hawk's argument — yet unshakeably firm in his compassion. Above all he is supremely self-sacrificing (त्यागी), ready to give his own flesh and even his whole body rather than abandon a helpless dove. His character embodies the chapter's title, 'करुणापरा हि साधवः'.

questions.question: Explain सन्धि with three examples from the lesson, and show the सन्धि-विच्छेद of each.
questions.answer: सन्धि is the merging or change of sounds when two words meet. (1) दीर्घ-सन्धि: when a short vowel meets a like vowel they combine into one long vowel — नागणयः = न + अगणयः (अ + अ = आ). (2) Another दीर्घ example: परोपकारार्थम् = परोपकार + अर्थम् (आ + अ = आ). (3) वृद्धि-सन्धि: चैव = च + एव (अ + ए = ऐ). In each case, sandhi-viccheda means splitting the joined form back into its original words, which is an essential skill for reading Sanskrit correctly.
questions.explanation: Three examples with splits and rule names.

questions.question: Using words from the lesson, explain the six common विभक्ति cases with one example each.
questions.answer: प्रथमा (nominative, subject): कपोतः 'the dove' (the doer). द्वितीया (accusative, object): मांसम् 'flesh' (what is given). तृतीया (instrumental, by/with): श्येनेन 'by the hawk'. चतुर्थी (dative, for): परोपकाराय 'for the good of others'. षष्ठी (genitive, of): कपोतस्य 'of the dove'. सप्तमी (locative, in/at): अङ्के 'in the lap'. Each ending changes the noun's role in the sentence; recognising them is the key to understanding Sanskrit.

questions.question:
Read and answer:
पुरा उशीनरदेशे शिबिः नाम राजा आसीत्। सः महान् दयालुः सत्यवादी धार्मिकश्च आसीत्। 'शरणागतस्य रक्षणं राज्ञः परमः धर्मः' इति सः अमन्यत।
(a) In which country did the king rule? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'दयालुः'. (c) What did the king consider his highest duty? (d) What is the moral?
questions.answer: (a) In उशीनर (Ushinara). (b) दयालुः = compassionate. (c) The protection of one who seeks refuge (शरणागत-रक्षा). (d) Moral: a true king (and a good person) puts compassion and the protection of the helpless above all else.

questions.question:
Read and answer:
अग्निः कपोतः अभवत्, इन्द्रः च श्येनः अभवत्। श्येनेन भीतः कपोतः राज्ञः अङ्के पतित्वा 'हे राजन्, मां रक्ष' इति अवदत्।
(a) What did Agni and Indra become? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'भीतः'. (c) Where did the dove fall for refuge? (d) In which विभक्ति is 'श्येनेन'?
questions.answer: (a) Agni became a dove (कपोत) and Indra a hawk (श्येन). (b) भीतः = frightened. (c) Into the king's lap (अङ्के). (d) श्येनेन is तृतीया (instrumental) — 'by the hawk'.

questions.question:
Read and answer:
श्येनः अवदत् — 'हे राजन्, अयं कपोतः मम आहारः। क्षुधार्तः अहम्। मम भोजनं मा अपहर।'
(a) What did the hawk claim about the dove? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'क्षुधार्तः'. (c) What did the hawk ask the king not to do? (d) Why was the king's position difficult?
questions.answer: (a) The hawk claimed the dove was its natural food (आहार). (b) क्षुधार्तः = tormented by hunger. (c) Not to take away (अपहर) its food. (d) It was difficult because protecting the dove and not starving the hawk are both duties (dharma).

questions.question:
Read and answer:
राजा तुलाम् आनाययत्। एकस्मिन् पात्रे कपोतः, अपरस्मिन् पात्रे राजा स्वमांसं स्थापयति स्म। परन्तु कपोतः सर्वदा गुरुः एव आसीत्।
(a) What did the king bring? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'गुरुः' here. (c) What was placed on the two pans? (d) What does the dove always weighing more suggest?
questions.answer: (a) A balance (तुला). (b) गुरुः here = heavy. (c) The dove on one pan, the king's own flesh on the other. (d) It suggests the test demanded ever greater sacrifice — his compassion had to be complete.

questions.question:
Read and answer:
परोपकाराय फलन्ति वृक्षाः परोपकाराय वहन्ति नद्यः।
परोपकाराय दुहन्ति गावः परोपकारार्थमिदं शरीरम्॥
(a) Why do trees bear fruit? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'नद्यः'. (c) Translate 'परोपकाराय दुहन्ति गावः'. (d) What is the central theme?
questions.answer: (a) Trees bear fruit for the good of others (परोपकाराय). (b) नद्यः = rivers. (c) 'Cows give milk for the good of others.' (d) Central theme: परोपकार — service to others is the purpose of life.

questions.question:
Read and answer:
अष्टादशपुराणेषु व्यासस्य वचनद्वयम्।
परोपकारः पुण्याय पापाय परपीडनम्॥
(a) Whose two statements are these? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'परपीडनम्'. (c) What leads to पुण्य (merit)? (d) What is the moral?
questions.answer: (a) The two statements of the sage Vyasa (from the eighteen Puranas). (b) परपीडनम् = harming/tormenting others. (c) परोपकार (helping others) leads to merit. (d) Moral: do good to others and harm none — this is the essence of all scripture.

questions.question:
Read and answer:
श्रूयतां धर्मसर्वस्वं श्रुत्वा चैवावधार्यताम्।
आत्मनः प्रतिकूलानि परेषां न समाचरेत्॥
(a) What is called धर्मसर्वस्व? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'परेषाम्'. (c) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'चैव'. (d) State the moral in one sentence.
questions.answer: (a) The essence of all dharma. (b) परेषाम् = towards/to others. (c) चैव = च + एव. (d) Moral: do not do to others what you would dislike being done to yourself (the golden rule).

questions.question:
Read and answer:
मातृवत् परदारेषु परद्रव्येषु लोष्टवत्।
आत्मवत् सर्वभूतेषु यः पश्यति स पण्डितः॥
(a) How should one regard others' wealth? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'आत्मवत्'. (c) Who is called a पण्डित here? (d) What value does the verse teach?
questions.answer: (a) As a mere clod of earth (लोष्टवत्), i.e. with no greed. (b) आत्मवत् = like oneself. (c) One who sees all beings as his own self. (d) Value: compassion and non-greed — treating all beings as oneself is true wisdom.

questions.question:
Read and answer:
राजा 'मा भैषीः, अहं त्वां रक्षिष्यामि' इति कपोतम् अवदत्।
(a) What did the king tell the dove not to do? (b) What पुरुष/वचन is 'रक्षिष्यामि'? (c) Give the प्रथमा एकवचन of कपोत. (d) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'रक्ष'.
questions.answer: (a) Not to fear (मा भैषीः). (b) रक्षिष्यामि is उत्तमपुरुष एकवचन (first person singular, future). (c) कपोतः. (d) रक्ष = protect (imperative 'protect!').

questions.question:
Read and answer:
शरणागतरक्षणे त्वं देहम् अपि नागणयः। तव करुणा अतुला।
(a) What did the king not count/consider? (b) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'नागणयः'. (c) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'अतुला'. (d) What quality of the king is praised?
questions.answer: (a) His own body (देह) — he did not count even his own body. (b) नागणयः = न + अगणयः. (c) अतुला = incomparable/unmatched. (d) His incomparable compassion (करुणा) and self-sacrifice.
